heading: INT. DINING CAR - END OF THE LINE - NIGHT

units.text: INT. DINING CAR - END OF THE LINE - NIGHT
White tablecloths, a single wilted carnation per table.
The train has stopped.
Beyond the glass, a snow-heavy platform and no station.
HELOISE DUVAL (30s, in a green coat, ring on a chain around her neck) stares into a cold cup of tea.
Across the table sits MATILDA ROSS (30s, in a gray traveling suit, her bag already packed).
She turns her own ring, a plain band, round and round on her finger.
Between them the carnation lies where somebody has dropped it.
She slides the ring off.
She sets it down.
She nudges it with a fingertip until it touches the other.
You'll want to keep that.
units.name: HELOISE

units.text: I'll want a lot of things.
units.name: MATILDA

units.text: A door hisses open at the end of the car.
ARCHIBALD PENNYWHISTLE (70s, conductor, white mustache, lantern, ticket punch) steps inside, stamping snow from his boots.
He takes in the table, the rings, the two silent women, and removes his cap with great gentleness.
Ladies. I regret to say this is the final stop.
units.name: ARCHIBALD

units.text: We know.
units.name: HELOISE

units.text: There is a bus. It leaves at dawn.
units.name: ARCHIBALD

units.text: Which way?
units.name: MATILDA

units.text: Both, I believe. It goes in one direction, and returns in the other.
units.name: ARCHIBALD

units.text: Heloise laughs, a short broken sound.
Matilda picks up her bag.
Archibald puts his cap back on, tips it, and tactfully retreats, leaving the door open behind him so the cold can come in.
